entries.text: v4.7.0 is the next minor release. 📣 Some news 🧪 Try Nitro v3 today You can now build your Nuxt 4 app with Nitro v3 (#37101). Nitro v3 is what Nuxt 5 is built on, so this is a way to move your server code (and your modules) over before you upgrade Nuxt itself. There's no config to change. Just add nitro to your dependencies: npm install nitro If nitro is in your package.json, Nuxt builds with Nitro v3. To go back, just remove it. Caution This is highly experimental. Nitro v3 is still a release candidate, and there are no guarantees. Please try it on a branch, not in production. 🙏 Do give Nitro v3 a try! On our benchmark app with about 170 pages, the same app on 4.7 served 33% more requests per second on its home page with Nitro v3 than with Nitro v2 (926 to 1,236), and 44% more on a page with 1,000 links (219 to 316), with identical HTML. On Nuxt 4, Nitro v3 runs with a compatibility layer, nitroLegacy, which keeps imports from h3, nitropack and #imports resolving, keeps the Nitro v2 auto-imports, useRuntimeConfig(event), event.node and the Nitro v2 hooks working, and keeps a long list of h3 v1 behaviours. Once things work, set nitroLegacy: false to find the code that still depends on it. A few things change with Nitro v3 regardless. The main one is route rules: /blog/* now also applies to /blog/2026/hello. Nuxt warns about each rule whose meaning changes (NUXT_B4029), and stops on a rule with more than one wildcard, like /api/*/items/**, which you can rewrite with a named par

entries.text: 4.6.4 is a security release. It fixes eight advisories in Nuxt and pulls in nitropack 2.13.6, which fixes three more in Nitro. We recommend upgrading as soon as you can. ⚠️ Behaviour changes These probably won't affect most apps, but it's worth flagging anyway: Error details in production. When a page fails to render on the server, the error page and the payload now only carry message and data of errors you create with createError. Everything else is stripped. Dev server Host checks. Webpack and rspack dev servers now reject requests with an unexpected Host header, as Vite already does. If you use a custom hostname or tunnel, you'll need to add it to the new devServer.allowedHosts option. workspaceDir detection. When workspaceDir isn't set, Nuxt now only widens it past rootDir to an explicit workspace root or the closest git repository. Nitropack cached routes. cache, swr and isr route rules now only cache GET and HEAD requests, and no longer store responses that set a cookie or send Cache-Control: private or no-store. Wildcard proxy and redirect rules also reject requests whose resolved target would leave the rule's scope. Route rules and encoded slashes. Route rules now match paths that contain encoded slashes, so /api%2Fadmin is covered by a /api/** rule. 👉 Changelog compare changes 🩹 Fixes nitro,nuxt: require unrouting 0.3.2 (768d21368) nitro: preserve wildcard tails in case-insensitive route rules (bf31e4cd8) nitro: require nitropack 2.13.6 (1b13c6981) nitro: keep leadin

entries.text: v4.6.0 is the next minor release. 📣 Some news 🖥️ Nuxt CLI v4 Alongside the release of Nuxt v4.6, today also brings a new major release of the Nuxt CLI: @nuxt/cli v4. It ships as a dependency of nuxt, so you'll get it automatically when you upgrade. Most of what's new is in nuxt dev: an interactive terminal UI, showing URLs, startup progress and keyboard shortcuts, with panels to dive into error logs, routes, network requests and more the dev server gives you more info, such as why it reloaded or restarted, which nuxt.config keys changed, where the time went during a slow start or build, and how long each module took to set up a CLI-level error channel rendered with my-bad (see below), powering things like automatically reloading when a syntax error in nuxt.config.ts is fixed a lock file in .nuxt/, which lets a second nuxt dev (say, one started by an agent) take over or defer to the one you started, and powers new nuxt curl and nuxt task commands that talk to the running server There's also a new nuxt docs "<query>" search, and nuxt preview --takeover can replace a running preview server. entries.text: ⚠️ This is a security release. We recommend upgrading as soon as possible with npx nuxt upgrade --dedupe. It fixes server-side RCE and unauthorized component instantiation via server island props, a route rule authorization bypass, server component DoS, cross-user payload disclosure on cached pages, and dev server path disclosure. Refreshing your lockfile also pulls in @nuxt/devtools@3.3.1, which fixes a separate critical development-only RCE. If you already upgraded for the earlier route rule advisory (CVE-2026-53721), you still need this release: one of the fixes addresses a regression introduced by that fix. If you use the cache, swr or isr route rules, purge any CDN or edge cache after upgrading; a leaked _payload.json may already be cached upstream.
